RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r1.speaker: الكفار
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r1.claim: One explanation is that they objected that Muhammad matched them in outward and inward qualities, lineage, appearance, and form, so they wondered how he alone received such rank.

RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, “from among them” underscores their ignorance: a man calls them to monotheism, honoring angels, the afterlife, and turning from worldly life, though they know he avoided lies; all of this should make them believe.
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r2.anchor: من هذه الكلمة لا التنبيه على كمال

RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r3.claim: Since Muhammad shared their clan and worldly circumstances, their refusal to obey and their amazement at his distinction had no cause except envy.
RAZI-FULL:v26p154#2/r3.anchor: فما كان لهذا التعجب سبب إلا الحسد

RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r1.claim: The wording “the disbelievers said,” rather than “they said,” heightens the astonishment and marks the accusation as speech born only of complete disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r1.anchor: إظهارا للتعجب ودلالة على أن هذا القول

RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r2.claim: Calling Muhammad a sorcerer and liar is incoherent: a sorcerer turns people from God to Satan, whereas Muhammad calls to God and reports truths established by reason, including resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r2.anchor: فإن الساحر هو الذي يمنع من طاعة الله ويدعو إلى طاعة الشيطان وهو عندكم بالعكس من ذلك والكذاب هو الذي يخبر عن الشيء لا على ما هو عليه

RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155/r3.claim: Rāzī groups the disbelievers’ attempted proofs of Muhammad’s falsehood under theology, prophethood, and the resurrection.

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r1.claim: As in 50:2, the disbelievers marvel that God chose a prophet from among them, either without prior high social standing or as a human rather than an angel.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r1.anchor: Here and in the almost identical 50:2, the incredulity of the idolaters is directed toward God for having chosen as a prophet either someone

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r2.claim: Other verses describing their marvel at this phenomenon are 7:69 and 10:2.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r2.anchor: For other verses that speak of their marveling at this phenomenon, see 7:69; 10:2.

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r3.claim: In deriding Muhammad, the disbelievers called him a sorcerer, an accusation also made against Moses and Jesus.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r3.anchor: In deriding the Prophet, the disbelievers labeled him a sorcerer (see also 10:2; 51:52), a charge also leveled against Moses

BURSEVI:v8p2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2/r1.claim: Meccan disbelievers rejected the arrival of a warner from their own people as outside possibility, seeing Muhammad as their equal in appearance, character, lineage, and social standing; they failed to wonder at their carved idols.
BURSEVI:v8p2/r1.anchor: عجب كفار أهل مكة من أن جاءهم منذر ينذرهم النار

BURSEVI:v8p2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2/r2.claim: Their inconsistent perplexity led them to accuse the Prophet of magic and lying.
BURSEVI:v8p2/r2.anchor: فلما تحيروا في شأن النبي عليه السلام نسبوه إلى السحر والكذب

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r1.claim: The explicit noun الكافرون replaces an expected pronoun to censure them and signal that only deeply immersed disbelievers would dare say this.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r1.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع المضمر غضبا عليهم وإيذانا بأنه لا يتجاسر على مثل ما يقولونه إلا المتوغلون في الكفر

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r2.claim: They call the warner a magician for the wonders he displays and a great liar for claiming that God sent him revelation.

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r3.claim: The intensive form كذّاب preserves the rhyme and suits their claim that his lies concern every Quranic verse, unlike the comparatively rare display of wonders; lying about God is especially grave.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r3.anchor: ولأن الكذب على الله ليس كالكذب على غيره ولكثرة الكذب في زعمهم

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r4.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya says diseased hearts, estranged from truth, interpreted prophethood as magic and the truthful Prophet as a liar according to their distorted understanding.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r4.anchor: لما كانوا منحرفي مزاج القلوب لمرض نسيان الحق جاءت النبوة على مذاق عقولهم المتغيرة سحرا

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r5.claim: Kashifi says blindness of judgment mistakes the lights of revelation for sorcery and cannot distinguish the rays of truth from the darkness of falsehood.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي (جه تيره رايي كه أنوار لمعات وحى را أزتاريكىء سحر امتياز نكند

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r6.claim: The accompanying poem compares the denier to a bat that cannot perceive the sun, though its radiance illuminates the world.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r6.anchor: كشته طالع آفتابي أنيينين عالم فروز ديدة خفاش را يكذره ازوى نورته

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r7.claim: Recognition of prophethood and sainthood is easy for the divinely aided, whose hearts turn from everything besides God; those deprived of aid turn away from God and slander His prophets and saints.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r7.anchor: فإن قلوبهم ألفت الإعراض عن الله

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r8.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r8.claim: Junayd says affirming the mystics' knowledge counts as the lesser sainthood, distinct from the greater sainthood.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r8.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم الجنيد رضي الله عنه التصديق بعلمنا هذا ولاية

BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r9.speaker: اليافعي
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r9.claim: Yafi'i divides people into four grades: belief, knowledge, and taste; belief and knowledge without taste; belief alone; and none of the three, the last group slandering spiritual elect through estrangement from their way.
BURSEVI:v8p2#2/r9.anchor: قال اليافعي : والناس على أربعة أقسام : القسم الأول

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r1.claim: They marvel that a warner came from their own kind, since the idolaters deny that a human can be a messenger.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r1.anchor: أي تعجبوا من مجيء منذر من نوعهم بأن كان بشرا فإن الوثنية تنكر رسالة البشر

TABATABAI:38:4-6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r2.claim: They call the Prophet a sorcerer because they cannot produce anything like the Qur'an, and a liar because they claim he falsely attributes its truths to God.
TABATABAI:38:4-6/r2.anchor: يرمونه بالسحر لكونهم عاجزين عن الإتيان بمثل ما أتى به وهو القرآن

TABRISI:38:2-5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:2-5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:2-5/r11.claim: They were astonished that a messenger from among them came from God to warn them against sins and the Fire.
TABRISI:38:2-5/r11.anchor: أي جاءهم رسول من أنفسهم مخوف من جهة الله تعالى يحذرهم المعاصي وينذرهم النار

TABRISI:38:2-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:2-5/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:2-5/r12.claim: They called Muhammad a sorcerer and liar because he claimed to be God's messenger.

THALABI:v8p178/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r4.claim: Umar's conversion distressed Quraysh and pleased believers; al-Walid convened twenty-five leading Quraysh notables, named in a roster.
THALABI:v8p178/r4.anchor:
وذلك
أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أسلم فشق ذلك على قريش وفرح به المؤمنون، فقال الوليد بن المغيرة للملأ من قريش

THALABI:v8p178/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r5.claim: The roster starts with al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jamil ibn Hisham, Ubayy and Umayya ibn Khalaf, Umar ibn Wahb, and Utba and Shayba ibn Rabi'a.
THALABI:v8p178/r5.anchor: وكانوا خمسة وعشرين رجلا، الوليد بن المغيرة وهو أكبرهم سنا، وأبو جميل ابن هشام، وأبي وأمية ابنا خلف، وعمر بن وهب بن خلف،

THALABI:v8p178/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r6.claim: Other listed leaders include Abd Allah ibn Umayya, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Harith and Adi ibn Qays, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and Abu al-Bukhturi.
THALABI:v8p178/r6.anchor: وعتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة، وعبد الله بن أمية والعاص بن وائل، والحرث بن قيس، وعدي بن قيس، والنضر بن الحرث، وأبو البحتري بن هشام،

THALABI:v8p178/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r7.claim: The remaining roster names Qart ibn Amr, Amir ibn Khalid, Makhrama ibn Nawfal, Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Akhnas, Huwaytib, Nabih and Munabbih, al-Walid ibn Utba, Hisham, and Suhayl.
THALABI:v8p178/r7.anchor: وقرط بن عمرو، وعامر بن خالد، ومحرمة بن نوفل، وزمعة بن الأسود، ومطعم بن عدي، والأخنس بن سريق، وحويطب ابن عبد العزى،

THALABI:v8p178/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r8.claim: Al-Walid sends the council to Abu Talib, who they ask to arbitrate between them and Muhammad.
THALABI:v8p178/r8.anchor: فقال لهم الوليد بن المغيرة: امشوا إلى أبي طالب. فأتوا أبا طالب فقالوا له: أنت شيخنا وكبيرنا،

THALABI:v8p178/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r9.claim: Abu Talib summons Muhammad and asks him to treat his people fairly rather than favoring his side completely.
THALABI:v8p178/r9.anchor: فأرسل أبو طالب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدعاه فقال له: يا ابن أخ هؤلاء قومك يسألونك السواء فلا تمل كل الميل على قومك.

THALABI:v8p178/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178/r10.claim: Quraysh asks Muhammad to reject them and their gods, promising to leave him and his God alone.
THALABI:v8p178/r10.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وماذا يسألوني؟» فقال: يقولون ارفضنا وارفض ذكر آلهتنا وندعك وإلهك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r1.claim: Al-Nazzam connects وعجبوا by coordination to الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق; وكم أهلكنا is an intervening clause and not part of the accusative construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r1.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: هذا منظوم بقوله: {بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق}؛ لأنه منسوق عليه بالواو.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the warner is a messenger from among the Meccans themselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) ومقاتل (¬2): يعني رسولا من أنفسهم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r3.claim: The disbelievers mentioned are the people of Mecca.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r4.claim: They call him a magician because they claim he separates family members and spouses by turning one toward him and away from the other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r4.anchor: {هذا ساحر} يفرق بين الإثنين بسحره، يعني: بين الولد ووالده والرجل وزوجته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p151/r5.claim: They call him a liar because he claims to be a messenger.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r6.claim: Those who marveled were the people of Mecca, and their warner from among them was Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:1-6/r6.anchor: يعني: أهل مكة { أن جاءهم منذر منهم } محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ELMALILI:38:1-14/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r1.claim: A report says that during Abu Talib’s illness, Quraysh complained about Muhammad’s attacks on their gods; he offered one word for Arab submission and Persian tribute, named the testimony of God’s oneness, and they recoiled, prompting this passage’s revelation.
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r1.anchor: Ebû Tâlib hastalandığı zaman Kureyşten bir heyet geldi, içlerinde Ebû Cehil de vardı.

ELMALILI:38:1-14/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r16.claim: In his rendering, an admonisher from among them is a prophet who awakens them, and the unbelievers call him a sorcerer and liar.
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r16.anchor: İçlerinden kendilerine uyandırıcı bir peygamber geldiğine şaştılar da dediler ki kâfirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r2.claim: The polytheists were astonished that a human from among them could be a prophet and accused him of being a sorcerer and liar.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r2.anchor: müşrikler, kendi aralarından, yani kendileri gibi beşerî özellikler taşıyan birinin peygamber olmasını şaşkınlıkla karşılayıp onu büyücü ve yalancı olmakla suçladılar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r3.claim: They thought a messenger from God should be an angel rather than a human, or at least should be selected from the Arabs' wealthiest or highest-status people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:3/r3.anchor: Akıllarınca eğer Allah katından bir elçi, bir uyarıcı gelecekse bu bir beşer değil, melek olmalıydı

BURHAN:v3p135/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p135/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p135/r6.claim: In these reports of opponents' words, the subject pronoun he is omitted before the predicate or accusation.

NAHHAS:v3p454/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r8.claim: أن جاءهم is accusative, with the sense من أن جاءهم.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r8.anchor: 4 في موضع نصب والمعنى من أن جاءهم

SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r1.claim: أن جاءهم has implied من, a disputed construction.
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r1.anchor: أي: من أن، وفيها الخلاف المشهور.

SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r2.claim: Calling them الكافرون in place of a pronoun testifies against their blameworthy description.
SAMIN-DURR:38:4/r2.anchor: من باب وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر شهادة عليهم بهذا الوصف القبيح

ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r7.claim: ʿUjāb means ʿajīb; the form is supported by usage such as karīm and karām for a man.
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r7.anchor: في معنى عجيب، ويجوز (عجاب) في معنى عجيب يقال: رجل كريم وكرام

ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.claim: When Abu Talib was dying, Quraysh complained of the Prophet; he offered a confession that would win Arab obedience and non-Arab tribute, Abu Jahl mocked the offer, and they left urging one another to cling to their gods.
ZAJJAJ:v4p320/r8.anchor: هذه حكاية عن ملأ من قريش لما مرض أبو طالب المرضة التي مات فيها

ASAD-NOTES:38:4#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:38:4#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:38:4#n7/r1.claim: Though initially describing Quraysh's response to Muhammad, the passage addresses a recurring reluctance to accept a human being from one's own community as divinely inspired.
ASAD-NOTES:38:4#n7/r1.anchor: the attitude of the pagan Quraysh towards the Prophet, it touches upon the reluctance of most people, at all times, to recognize

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.claim: Like the previous sūrahs in this group, Ṣād is founded on tawḥīd; Quraysh oppose its reminder from arrogance and polytheism and will believe only when it is too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.anchor: Like the previous sūrahs of this group, this sūrah is also based on tawh@īd.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.claim: Verses 1–11 present the Qur’an as a reminder rejected from arrogance, paralleling earlier nations; Quraysh too will believe only after seeing their fate, when faith is useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.anchor: This Qur’ān is a reminder for people; however, because of arrogance and haughtiness they are opposing it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.claim: Quraysh cannot accept a messenger from among themselves, so they call him sorcerer and liar; their leaders rally people to defend idols and ancestral religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.anchor: They are not able to digest the fact that a person from among them, as God’s messenger, should warn them of the fate of polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p479/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p479/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p479/r6.claim: The Quraysh marvel that a human being from among them was made God’s warner, and ask why the messenger was not a chief from Mecca or Ṭāʾif rather than a poor man.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p479/r6.anchor: why was someone from among them given this status? And if at all this was to be done, why did God select a poor person for this?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r1.claim: The objection that a human was made messenger is addressed in verse 4; the complaint that the chosen man was poor appears in verse 8. Both express the conceit named in verse 2.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r1.anchor: This verse refers to the first of these reasons. In verse eight ahead, the second of these reasons is mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r2.claim: Arrogance and haughtiness lead the disbelievers to call God’s messenger a sorcerer and a liar.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r2.anchor: it is because of their arrogance and haughtiness that these disbelievers regard God’s messenger to be a sorcerer and a liar.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r3.claim: Unable to refute the Qur’an’s miraculous eloquence, the Quraysh label it sorcery to keep its effect from persuading the masses to accept it as God’s word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r3.anchor: The Quraysh could not refute the miraculous eloquence of the Qur’ān; however, they did not want it to influence their masses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r4.claim: They explain the discourse’s sway as the work of a word magician rather than divine revelation, and also call the Qur’an poetry and the Prophet a poet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r4.anchor: they would regard the Qur’ān as sorcery and the Prophet (sws) as a sorcerer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r5.claim: Kadhdhāb means a liar and braggart.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r5.anchor: The word ابٌ َّذَك means a person whose is a liar and a bragger.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r6.claim: The insult suggests that, although a word magician, Muhammad falsely claims revelation and a commission to warn; the Quraysh’s real aversion is his claim to prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r6.anchor: though this person is a magician of words but to bluff the masses he claims that whatever he says is revealed to him from God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r7.claim: The verse’s style expresses sorrow: God sent them a warner from their own people and a reminder-filled book, yet their conceit makes them mock him as sorcerer and liar.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p480/r7.anchor: The style of this verse bears witness that it expresses sorrow at these unfortunate people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p135/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p135/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p135/r16.claim: The proposed answer is reinforced by the warning of a messenger here and Yasin's warning to a people; messengership entails warning and good news.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p135/r16.anchor: ويقوي هذا التقدير ذكر النذارة هنا في قوله: وعجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم، وقال هناك: لتنذر قوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r8.claim: After describing unbelievers' arrogance and opposition, the passage gives their corrupt accusations of sorcery and lying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r8.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى عن الكفار أنهم في عزة وشقاق، أردف بما صدر عنهم من كلماتهم الفاسدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r9.claim: The explicit noun الكافرون replaces a pronoun to highlight the trait that led them to call the messenger sorcerer and liar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r9.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع المضمر في قوله: وقال الكافرون، أي: وقالوا تنبيها على الصفة التي أوجبت لهم العجب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r12.claim: The pronoun in وعجبوا refers to the unbelievers, who found it strange that a messenger arose from among them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p137/r12.anchor: والضمير في وعجبوا لهم، أي استغربوا مجيء رسول من أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r1.claim: Their astonishment is among the false claims that follow from arrogance and opposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r1.anchor: حكاية لأباطيلهم المتفرعة على ما حكاه من استكبارهم وشقاقهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r2.claim: They treat it as impossible that a messenger be their kind as a human or from their time and community, known for illiteracy; their wonder expresses emphatic denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r2.anchor: أي عجبوا من أن جاءهم رسول من جنسهم أي بشرا أو من عهدهم وهم معروفون بالأمية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r3.claim: The explicit noun replaces a pronoun to condemn them, indicating only the deeply entrenched in unbelief and sin would dare say this.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r3.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع الضمير غضبا عليهم وذما لهم وإيذانا بأنه لا يتجاسر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r4.claim: They call him a sorcerer because of signs he manifests that they cannot match.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r4.anchor: فيما يظهره مما لا نستطيع له مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r5.claim: They call him a liar for claiming that God sent and revealed to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p165/r5.anchor: فيما يسنده إلى ألله عز وجل من الإرسال والإنزال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r1.speaker: المدخل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r1.claim: Al-Madkhal says the first opinion-based exegesis report, if authentic, condemns bypassing the proper sources: return word meanings to linguists, abrogation to reports, and intended meaning to the Prophet; where these offer no answer, evidence-based reasoning is allowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r1.anchor: الطريق الرجوع في تفسير ألفاظه إلى أهل اللغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r2.speaker: المدخل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r2.claim: Alternatively, the warning targets those who make their doctrine or desire primary and force the Quran to support it; the preposition in the report then denotes causal opinion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r2.anchor: أو أراد من قال بالقرآن قولا يوافق هواه بأن يجعل المذهب أصلا والتفسير تابعا له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r3.speaker: المدخل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r3.claim: The warning may concern ambiguous passages whose meaning God alone knows, or asserting God’s intended meaning categorically without proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r3.anchor: أو يقال ذلك في المتشابه الذي لا يعلمه إلا الله أو في الجزم بأن مراد الله تعالى كذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r4.claim: The second hadith can mean that one who speaks without knowledge about a difficult Quranic question risks divine anger, or that one who knowingly states a false interpretation faces the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r4.anchor: وأما الحديث الثاني فله معنيان الأول من قال في مشكل القرآن بما لا يعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says Quranic commands to refer questions to qualified investigators and to ponder the text support reasoned exegesis, citing 4:83, 47:24, and 38:29.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r5.anchor: ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r6.claim: He cites Ibn Abbas’s report that the Quran is pliable and multivalent and should be read in its best sense, the Prophet’s prayer that Ibn Abbas learn religion and interpretation, and Ali’s denial that the Prophet gave the family hidden scripture beyond the written text and understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r6.anchor: القرآن ذلول ذو وجوه فأحملوه على أحسن وجوهه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r7.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that understanding Quranic constructions depends entirely on transmitted exegesis, since commentators differ widely and Prophetic explanations of such meanings are exceptionally rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r7.anchor: والعجب كل العجب مما يزعم أن علم التفسير مضطر إلى النقل في فهم معاني التراكيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r8.claim: Qualified interpretation belongs to someone deeply versed in Arabic, spiritual discernment, and religious sciences, who recognizes Quranic inimitability directly and can reach its deeper meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r8.anchor: من كان متبحرا في علم اللسان مترقيا منه إلى ذوق العرفان وله في رياض العلوم الدينية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r9.claim: Those absorbed in Aristotelian speculations and preferring thorns to peacock feathers cannot grasp the Quran’s subtleties and wonders.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r9.anchor: وأما من صرف عمره بوساوس أرسطاطاليس وأختار شوك القنافذ على ريش الطواويس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r10.claim: Sufi readings disclose subtle allusions to practitioners and can accord with the intended outward meanings; they do not replace the apparent sense with a hidden one, a doctrine Al-Alusi attributes to esoteric heretics who seek to abolish the law.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r10.anchor: يمكن التطبيق بينها وبين الظواهر المرادة وذلك من كمال الإيمان ومحض العرفان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r11.claim: Al-Alusi says Sufi masters themselves urged preservation of the outward exegesis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p6/r11.anchor: كيف وقد حضوا على حفظ التفسير الظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p71/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p71/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p71/r1.claim: Those who were astonished are the disbelievers mentioned earlier; they objected that a warner and messenger came from among themselves and called him a lying magician.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p71/r1.anchor: يعني: الكفار الذين ذكرهم الله عز وجل في قوله: "بل الذين كفروا"

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.claim: They are astonished that a warner came from among them, either a human like them or an unlettered member of their own people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.anchor: بشر مثلهم أو أمي من عدادهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.claim: Calling them “the unbelievers” instead of using a pronoun rebukes them and signals that their disbelief emboldened this statement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع الضمير غضبا عليهم وذما لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.claim: They call the miracle he displays magic and his claims about God lies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.anchor: فيما يظهره معجزة. { كذاب } فيما يقوله على الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.claim: After ʿUmar accepted Islam, Quraysh were distressed and appealed to Abū Ṭālib to settle matters with his nephew. The Prophet asked what they wanted; they demanded he abandon them and their idols, offering to leave him and his God alone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.anchor: لما أسلم عمر رضي الله عنه شق ذلك على قريش

BIQAI-FULL:v6p357/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p357/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p357/r15.claim: God discloses truth both through the created world and through speech; revelation is the clearer account, and rejecting it makes the arrogant liable to destruction, as shown in the following account of ruined warners.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p357/r15.anchor: فأما الحال فهو ما تنطق به أحوال الموجودات التي أبدعها سبحانه في هذا الكون من علوم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r7.claim: A human warner from their own people, Arabs, and Quraysh should not surprise them: familiarity makes him better known, more credible, and more readily heard.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r7.anchor: فإن كون النذير بما يحل من المصائب من القوم المنذرين - مع كونه أشرف لهم - أقعد في النذارة لأنهم أعرف به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r8.claim: He is called a warner in the active participle rather than an intensive form because their surprise concerned his mere warning, not its degree.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r8.anchor: من مطلق نذارته لا مبالغته فيها أتى باسم الفاعل دون فعيل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r9.claim: The conjunction wāw separates their magician accusation from their surprise because it is a distinct charge, not a consequence of that surprise.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r9.anchor: معبرًا بالواو دون الفاء لأن وصفهم له بالسحر ليس شبيه هذا العجب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r10.claim: Calling them “the unbelievers” rather than using a pronoun shows that they knowingly concealed truth and were stubborn deniers, not ignorant or heedless.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r10.anchor: فهم جاحدون لا جاهلون , ومعاندون لا غافلون

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r11.claim: They called him a magician because his miraculous words and deeds attracted hearts, and sorcery was their nearest accusation; they avoided an intensive form that might draw people to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r11.anchor: وكان أقرب ما يقدحون به فيه السحر قذفوه به ولم يعبروا بصيغة مبالغة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r12.claim: Their shameless intensive charge contradicts their former name for him, al-Amīn; nothing had changed except his increasingly truthful speech and evident moral excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p358/r12.anchor: وأتوا بوقاحة بصيغة المبالغة وقد كانوا قبل ذلك يسمونه الأمين وهو يعلمون أنه لم يتجدد له شيء إلا إيتانه بأصدق الصدق

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r1.claim: Qatada says the polytheists marveled that Muhammad came as a warner from among them and rejected the call to one God, claiming one deity could not hear all their needs.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {وعجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم} يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r1.claim: The explicit label ‘the disbelievers’ replaces the expected pronoun to brand them as unbelievers in response to their branding the Prophet; kufr sums up corrupt thought and deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r1.anchor: وهذا لقصد وصفهم بأنهم كافرون بربهم مقابلة لما وصموا به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r2.claim: The demonstrative refers to the Prophet and is used contemptuously, as in the question ‘Is this the one who mentions your gods?’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r2.anchor: أشاروا به إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استعملوا اسم الإشارة لتحقير مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r3.claim: They uttered the accusation as they left the gathering at Abū Ṭālib mentioned in the sura’s occasion of revelation; their recent encounter made the Prophet seem present as they pointed to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r3.anchor: وإنما قالوا مقالتهم هذه حين انصرافهم من مجلس أبي طالب المذكور في سبب نزول السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r4.claim: They called incomprehensible claims such as one God or resurrection sorcery, since they associated magic with unintelligible speech, and called the understandable but impossible claim of prophethood a lie; they explain the charge through monotheism and the question of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p209/r4.anchor: لأنهم لما لم تقبل عقولهم ما كلمهم به زعموا ما لا يفهمون منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p102/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p102/r1.claim: The people astonished are the unbelievers, and the warner from among them is a messenger warning them of the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p102/r1.anchor: يعني الكفار ﴿ أن جاءهم منذر منهم ﴾ يعني رسولا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p53/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p53/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p53/r1.claim: The polytheists marvel that their warner is a human like them and call him a sorcerer and liar, echoing the objection cited from Jonah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p53/r1.anchor: مخبرا عن المشركين في تعجبهم من بعثة الرسول بشرا، كما قال تعالى

MUQATIL:38:1-4/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r6.claim: The Meccans were amazed that Muhammad, one of them, came as a messenger warning them.
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r6.anchor: { وعجبوا أن جاءهم } محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { منذر منهم } رسول منهم

MUQATIL:38:1-4/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r7.speaker: الكافرون
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r7.claim: The Meccan unbelievers called the Prophet a sorcerer who separates people and a liar claiming to be a messenger.
MUQATIL:38:1-4/r7.anchor: { وقال الكافرون } من أهل مكة { هذا ساحر } يفرق بين الاثنين { كذاب } [آية: 4] يعنون النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r1.claim: The phrase means they wondered that a warner had come to them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ وعجبوا أن جاءهم ﴾ من أن جاءهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r2.claim: The warner is a messenger from among them sent to warn them; they found it implausible that the Prophet was human.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r2.anchor: رسول من أنفسهم بنذرهم يعنى استبعدوا أن يكون النبى من البشر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r3.claim: Calling them disbelievers rather than simply they expresses anger and shows only hardened unbelievers would dare this claim.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r3.anchor: ولم يقل وقالوا إظهار للغضب عليهم ودلالة على أن هذا القول لا يجسر عليه إلا الكافرون المتوغلون فى الكفر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r4.claim: They call one God confirmed a liar and magician, marvel at monotheistic truth, yet fail to marvel at false polytheism; no disbelief is more extreme.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p32#4/r4.anchor: إذ لا كفر أبلغ من أن يسموا من صدقه الله كاذبا ساحرا ويتعجبوا من التوحيد وهو الحق الأبلج

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.claim: An is accusative with the sense of min an, from the fact that a warner came to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r1.anchor: «أن» في موضع نصب والمعنى من أن جاءهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.claim: One parsing connects their astonishment to the preceding description of pride and discord, with the destruction phrase parenthetical.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r2.anchor: قيل: هو متصل بقوله: { في عزة وشقاق }

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.claim: An alternate reading begins a new statement: their astonishment at a warner from among them displays their ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r3.anchor: وقيل: لا بل هذا ابتداء كلام أي ومن جهلهم أنهم أظهروا التعجب

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r4.claim: Calling him a magician means that his deceptive speech tricks people.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r4.anchor: أي يجيء بالكلام المموه الذي يخدع به الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r5.claim: An alternate explanation is that they called him a magician because his magic separated parent from child and husband from wife.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r5.anchor: وقيل: يفرق بسحره بين الوالد وولده والرجل وزوجته

QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:4-5/r6.claim: They called him a liar in his claim to prophethood.
